cards.claim: There is no additional cost to run a DB instance in a VPC.
All new DB instances are created in the account's default VPC unless you specify otherwise.
You can have only one default subnet per Availability Zone, and you cannot create a default subnet in a nondefault VPC.
cards.scope: per Availability Zone, per default VPC; maximum.
links: [cannot create a default subnet in a nondefault VPC](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-default-subnet-one-per-az)
spoken: one default subnet per Availability Zone

cards.claim: A default VPC gets a /20 default subnet in each Availability Zone, each with up to 4,096 addresses, a few of which are reserved by AWS.
cards.scope: per default VPC; default; not adjustable.
spoken: a slash twenty subnet in every Availability Zone

cards.claim: In a VPC you can create a public-facing subnet with Internet access for web servers and place the backend RDS DB instances in a private-facing subnet with no Internet access.
cards.scope: RDS DB instances in a VPC.

cards.claim: A common pattern places web servers in a public subnet and the DB instances in a private subnet so that only the web servers can reach the databases.
The default quota for DB subnet groups is 50 per account in each Region (20 in ap-south-1), and it is adjustable.
cards.scope: per account, per Region; default; adjustable; ap-south-1 has a default of 20.

cards.claim: The default quota for DB parameter groups is 50 per account in each Region (20 in ap-south-1), and it is adjustable.
cards.scope: per account, per Region; default; adjustable; ap-south-1 has a default of 20.

cards.claim: A changed static parameter takes effect only after you manually reboot the DB instance; a changed dynamic parameter takes effect immediately by default, without a reboot.
links: [after you manually reboot the associated DB instances](../facts/rds.md#rds-parameter-static-dynamic)

cards.claim: By default, an account can have up to 40 DB instances in total.
cards.scope: per account, all RDS DB instances in total; default; adjustable.

cards.claim: VPC security groups control traffic in and out of a DB instance, and by default network access to a DB instance is turned off until security group rules allow it.
cards.scope: DB instance network access; default; adjustable.

cards.claim: A DB instance in a VPC always has a private IP address; the Public access option decides whether it also gets a public IP address, and public access still needs security group inbound rules and an internet gateway on the DB subnet group's subnets.
A DB parameter group is a container for engine configuration values that can be applied to one or more DB instances.
cards.scope: DB parameter groups and option groups.

cards.claim: All DB instances that use a DB parameter group get every parameter update made to that group.
cards.scope: DB parameter groups and option groups.

cards.claim: SSL/TLS encryption of connections is supported for all Amazon RDS engines, and RDS generates an SSL/TLS certificate for each DB instance.
cards.scope: encryption in transit (SSL/TLS) to RDS databases.

cards.claim: For RDS for MySQL, the require_secure_transport parameter forces SSL/TLS for all user connections; it is OFF by default and can be set to ON in the DB parameter group without a reboot.
links: [You don't need to reboot your DB instance](../facts/rds.md#rds-tls-force-mysql)

cards.claim: The AWS database decision guide says to use Amazon RDS when you need a fully managed relational database with a choice of six engines (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle and Db2); it is optimized for structured data with full SQL support, automated backups, software patching and Multi-AZ deployments.
cards.scope: AWS database decision guide (Choosing an AWS database service).

cards.claim: Amazon RDS can automatically back up your database and keep the database software up to date.
